<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Two people are killed and three others injured in [[Myitkyina]] after being shot in the head, as security forces open fire on people protesting against the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup d'état]] in [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/8/myanmar-2 (Al Jazeera)]
*Multiple people are injured by a [[homemade bomb]] accidentally [[detonating]] in a classroom at Newaygo High School in [[Newaygo, Michigan]], United States. [https://www.9and10news.com/2021/03/08/newaygo-high-school-explosion-investigation-continues/ (WWTV-TV)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**[[Myanmar]]'s [[State Administration Council]] revokes the licence of five media companies, namely Myanmar Now, Khit Thit Media, Democratic Voice of Burma (DVB), Mizzima, and 7Day, amidst the crackdown on press outlets covering [[2021 Myanmar protests|anti-coup protests]]. [https://www.voanews.com/east-asia-pacific/myanmar-military-strips-five-media-companies-licenses-0 (VOA)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[EuroAsia Interconnector]]<!-- There was a discussion on the talk page of Elijahandskip about this being a header and the news being in the 2nd line. Please do not change without seeing that discussion. -->
**[[Cyprus]], [[Greece]], and [[Israel]] sign an agreement to build the world's largest and deepest [[submarine power cable]] that will connect the three [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] countries' [[power grid]]s at a cost of about [[United States dollar|$]]900 million. The project is expected to be completed by 2024. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/economy/1156627/israel-cyprus-and-greece-agree-to-link-power-grids-via-subsea-cable/ (''Kathimerini'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Bata explosions]]
**The death toll from yesterday's explosions in [[Bata, Equatorial Guinea|Bata]], [[Equatorial Guinea]], rises to 98 people. More than 615 others are wounded. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/8/death-toll-from-devastating-equatorial-guinea-blasts-jumps-to-98 (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
*****Millions of students across [[England]] return to primary and secondary schools after two months studying at home during the third [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] as a first step towards a return to normality. [https://www.bbc.com/news/education-56293639 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19, becoming the second country in [[Europe]] to reach the milestone after the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210308-italy-s-coronavirus-death-toll-passes-100-000-with-cases-rising (France 24)]
****The [[regions of Italy|region]] of [[Campania]] enters a lockdown which is expected to end on March 21. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/03/08/covid-in-italy-three-more-regions-placed-under-tighter-restrictions (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****[[Austria]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.2 [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] first detected in [[Brazil]] in a person from [[Salzburg (federal state)|Salzburg]] state. [https://www.thelocal.at/20210307/thousands-turn-out-for-vienna-anti-lockdown-protest/ (''The Local Austria'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports its youngest death from [[COVID-19]]. The patient was a 37-day-old infant. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/greece-mourns-youngest-covid-victim-37-day-baby.856807 (''Times of Malta'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****[[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] extends the [[Netherlands|country]]'s strict lockdown until the end of the month and advises against foreign travel until April 15. The curfew from 9 p.m. to 4:30 a.m. will remain in place through the [[2021 Dutch general election|election]] on March 17, but those working or visiting a voting booth will not be fined for breaching it. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/dutch-prime-minister-extends-countrys-pandemic-lockdown-76326370 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in East Timor]]
****[[East Timor]] imposes a "sanitary fence and mandatory confinement" in the capital [[Dili]] for the next seven days beginning at midnight. This is the country's first lockdown since the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7158299/east-timor-imposes-first-virus-lockdown/ (''The Canberra Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] receives its first shipment of 1.1 million doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] supplied through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2021/03/08/indonesia-receives-first-astrazeneca-vaccines-under-covax-facility.html?fbclid=IwAR06lowXZvtVtmF8oPC5MZzwWmJmyvbeIVgbzwT8zSx-730RjGqvTV0nsCk (''The Jakarta Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 108 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,336. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-03/08/c_139793971.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****[[President of Syria|President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] and his wife [[Asma al-Assad]] both test positive for COVID-19, according to a statement from the presidential office. They are both reported to be in good health with "minor symptoms". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-syria-assad/syrias-president-assad-and-his-wife-test-positive-for-covid-19-statement-idUSKBN2B018K (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] begins a [[vaccination]] programme against COVID-19 starting with health workers in [[Hanoi]], [[Ho Chi Minh City]], and [[Hai Duong Province]] using the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://en.vietnamplus.vn/vietnam-begins-covid19-vaccination-on-march-8/197215.vnp (VietnamPlus)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hawaii]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Hawaii]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in [[South Africa]] in a person from [[Oahu, Hawaii|Oahu]] with no known travel history. [https://apnews.com/article/africa-south-africa-coronavirus-pandemic-honolulu-hawaii-1c4ecb70b6939b5981023748b1ab2a45 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Michigan]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in [[South Africa]] in a child from [[Jackson County, Michigan|Jackson County]]. [https://www.woodtv.com/health/coronavirus/south-african-virus-variant-found-in-michigan/ (WOOD-TV)]
***The U.S. surpasses 29 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.kiro7.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-29-million-death-toll-swells-past-525000/K3KQFU4ZWJGC3BRYWNTE252UEU/ (KIRO-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The [[government of Brazil|government]] announces a deal with [[Pfizer]] to receive 14 million doses of its [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccine]] by June, and a total of 99 million doses by the end of the year. [https://riotimesonline.com/brazil-news/miscellaneous/covid-19/brazil-to-get-extra-5-million-covid-19-doses-from-pfizer-economy-minister/ (''The Rio Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] announces that the [[New Zealand Government]] has secured 8.5 million doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccine, and that they have now secured enough vaccines to vaccinate the entire population of New Zealand. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/covid-19-coronavirus-prime-minister-jacinda-ardern-reveals-enough-pfizer-vaccines-for-every-new-zealander/BDEO4HPUGMPKKYO6A2FN4TIJHU/ (''The New Zealand Herald'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Killing of George Floyd]]
**The trial of former [[Minneapolis Police Department]] officer [[Derek Chauvin]] begins in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]]. Chauvin's trial is the first time that a judge in Minnesota has authorized cameras to show a full criminal trial. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/derek-chauvin-trial-george-floyd-b1813898.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Operation Car Wash]]
**Brazilian [[Supreme Federal Court]] Justice [[Edson Fachin]] rules that all convictions of former [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] must be nullified. This ruling restores Lula's political rights and thus clears the way for his [[2022 Brazilian general election|presidential candidacy in 2022]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210308-brazil-judge-overturns-ex-leader-lula-s-convictions (France 24)]
*A judge in [[Senegal]] releases opposition leader [[Ousmane Sonko]] on bail, after days of protests as a result of his arrest. Eight people died during the protests. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56323444 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2019–2021 Lebanese protests]]
**Protesters block all major roads leading to the capital [[Beirut]] amid continued unrest over the crash of the [[Lebanese pound|pound]], increase in consumer goods prices, mass [[unemployment]] and delay of the formation of a new [[Government of Lebanon|government]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/protesters-paralyze-lebanon-amid-political-economic-crisis-lebanon-protesters-saad-hariri-beirut-michel-aoun-b1813822.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Libyan Crisis (2011–present)|Libyan Crisis]], [[Libyan peace process]]
**[[High Council of State (Libya)|Parliament]] meets in the central city of [[Sirte]] to vote on the approval of the interim [[Government of National Unity (Libya)|Government of National Unity]], led by [[Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh]]. Voting is expected to take place tomorrow. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/8/libyan-parliament-meets-after-decade-of-war-to-debate-new-govt (Al Jazeera)]
